approach.summary: Add a `--json` Bool flag to cmdStats. After runs are read and sorted, and if the flag is set, call a new self-contained function in stats.go. That function builds typed structs for the runs and totals, using the same rules as the text totals (damaged runs are left out of the sums and by_status; spend is a lower bound if any run is damaged; tokens/cost are a lower bound if any run's usage is not ok or any run is damaged). It prints the result with json.MarshalIndent plus Fprintln, like `shogun status --json`, and returns before the tabwriter. The table code stays byte-for-byte as it is. The existing stats test is extended to run `stats --json` on the same fixture. The usage line and the README row gain `--json`.

alternatives.name: Refactor the table loop into a shared totals helper that both outputs use
alternatives.why_not: This touches the table path the task freezes and is a refactor the task does not ask for. A separate JSON builder keeps the plain output provably unchanged.

alternatives.name: Reuse run.Counters as the per-run JSON object
alternatives.why_not: Its omitempty token tags would drop zero fields. It also carries fields that are not in the table (logical_calls, wait_seconds, ...), so the JSON would not be the same data as the table.

steps.title: Add --json output to shogun stats
steps.objective: `shogun stats --json` prints the runs and totals as one JSON document, and the plain output is unchanged.
actions: In cmdStats (stats.go:40-41), add `asJSON := fs.Bool("json", false, "print the runs and totals as one JSON document")` next to the --dir flag.

Add the JSON types in stats.go. statsRunJSON has ID `id`, Status `status` and Damaged `damaged,omitempty`, plus an embedded pointer *statsUsageJSON that is nil for damaged runs, so its fields are omitted there. statsUsageJSON has Mode `mode`, Planner `planner`, Reviewer `reviewer`, Attempts int `attempts`, ActiveSeconds float64 `active_seconds`, InputTokens/CacheReadTokens/CacheWriteTokens/OutputTokens/ReasoningTokens int64 (`input_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`, all without omitempty), CostUSD float64 `cost_usd` and Usage `usage`. statsTotalsJSON has Runs int `runs`, ByStatus map[string]int `by_status`, Damaged int `damaged`, the same attempts/active_seconds/token/cost fields, SpendLowerBound bool `spend_lower_bound` and UsageLowerBound bool `usage_lower_bound`. The top-level document is {Runs []statsRunJSON `runs`; Totals statsTotalsJSON `totals`}.

Add `func (a *app) printStatsJSON(runs []runStats) int`. It loops over runs in their sorted order. For a damaged run (st == nil), it appends {id, status "damaged", damaged reason} and counts it. Otherwise it appends the usage object from r.mode, r.planner, r.reviewer (raw, no dash), st.Counters and r.usage(), increments ByStatus[string(st.Status)], and adds the counters to the totals the same way as stats.go:83-90. It sets SpendLowerBound = damaged > 0 and UsageLowerBound = (any run's usage != "ok") || damaged > 0. It initialises Runs as an empty slice and ByStatus as an empty map so they encode as [] and {}. It prints with `data, _ := json.MarshalIndent(doc, "", " ")` and `fmt.Fprintln(a.stdout, string(data))`, then returns ExitOK. Add "encoding/json" to the imports.

In cmdStats, if *asJSON, call a.printStatsJSON(runs) right after the sort at stats.go:59 and before the `len(runs) == 0` check. An empty run set then still prints a document (runs [] and zero totals) and nothing goes to stderr (assumption in Q-002). Do not change the lines from stats.go:60 onwards.

Update the usage line in main.go:87 to `shogun stats [--dir d] [--json]` and keep the column alignment. Add `--json` next to `--dir` in the README.md:237 stats row (e.g. '`--dir`, `--json` prints the same as one JSON document').

verification.expected: `git diff cmd/shogun/stats.go` shows no changed or removed lines in the table/totals printing block (the original lines 60-116). Only the flag, the JSON branch, the new types/function and the import are added.

risks.mitigation: encoding/json skips nil embedded struct pointers. The S-002 test asserts that the damaged run has no `attempts` key, so a wrong encoding would fail it.

questions.question: Are these JSON key names and this shape acceptable? The shape is {runs:[{id,status,mode,planner,reviewer,attempts,active_seconds,input_tokens,cache_read_tokens,cache_write_tokens,output_tokens,reasoning_tokens,cost_usd,usage,damaged?}], totals:{runs,by_status,damaged,attempts,active_seconds,input_tokens,cache_read_tokens,cache_write_tokens,output_tokens,reasoning_tokens,cost_usd,spend_lower_bound,usage_lower_bound}}.
questions.why: The key names become a public machine interface that scripts will rely on.
questions.impact: Renaming keys later breaks consumers. Choosing now only changes the struct tags and test assertions.
options: Use the proposed snake_case names, which match state.json
Use a single `lower_bound` flag for all totals
questions.proposed_assumption: Use the proposed names with two lower-bound flags. The text output already distinguishes attempts/time (lower bound only when runs are damaged) from tokens/cost (also when usage is missing).

questions.question: With --json and no runs in the directory, should stats print an empty document (runs [] and zero totals) or keep today's behaviour (a note on stderr and nothing on stdout)?
questions.why: The task does not cover the empty case. A JSON consumer usually expects a document every time.
questions.impact: This decides whether the JSON branch runs before or after the `len(runs) == 0` early return.
options: Print an empty document on stdout
Keep today's stderr note with empty stdout
questions.proposed_assumption: Print an empty document on stdout and no stderr note. Moving the JSON call below the early return would switch to the other option.
